answer:
Calculate the Darcy-Weisbach friction pressure drop for water flowing through a single straight horizontal pipe.
Pipe length is 100 m with an internal diameter of 50 mm.
The volumetric flow rate is 2 L/s (0.002 m³/s), giving an average velocity of approximately 1.02 m/s.
The working fluid is water at 20 °C with density ρ = 998 kg/m³ and dynamic viscosity μ = 1×10⁻³ Pa·s.
The pipe material is galvanized iron with an absolute roughness ε = 0.15 mm.
Compute the Reynolds number from the given velocity, diameter, density, and viscosity to characterize the flow regime.
Determine the Darcy friction factor using the Colebrook-White equation (or a validated approximation such as Swamee-Jain) with the relative roughness ε/D = 0.15/50 = 0.003.
Use the Darcy-Weisbach equation ΔP = f · (L/D) · (ρ·v²/2) to compute the pressure drop.
Report the pressure drop in Pascals and also express it in meters of water head and in bar for convenience.
Exclude all minor losses; only friction along the 100 m straight run is required.
State all intermediate values (Reynolds number, friction factor) used in the calculation.
